purpose: This medicine is used to treat bacterial infections such as ear infections, sinus infections, pneumonia, urinary tract infections, and skin infections. It works against bacteria that have become resistant to regular amoxicillin alone. Your doctor prescribed it because the infection you have needs this stronger combination to be cleared up properly.
how_it_works: Amoxicillin is an antibiotic that kills bacteria by breaking down their protective outer wall, causing them to fall apart. Some bacteria are sneaky and make a substance that destroys amoxicillin before it can work. Clavulanate blocks that defense mechanism, so the amoxicillin can do its job and wipe out the infection.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and stomach upset. You may also notice a skin rash. Taking this medicine with food can help reduce stomach problems. Diarrhea is more common with this medicine than with regular amoxicillin because of the clavulanate.
warnings: Stop taking this medicine and call your doctor right away if you get a severe rash, hives, swelling of your face or throat, or trouble breathing, as this could be a serious allergic reaction. Tell your doctor if you are allergic to penicillin or cephalosporin antibiotics. Let your doctor know if you have liver or kidney problems. This medicine can sometimes cause a serious type of diarrhea called C. difficile, so call your doctor if you have severe or persistent diarrhea. Always finish the full course of antibiotics even if you feel better.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is one tablet taken by mouth every 8 to 12 hours, depending on the strength your doctor prescribed. Always take it with a meal or snack to protect your stomach. Take it at the same times every day and finish all of your pills even if you start feeling better early. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for your next dose.
